findings.evidence: `EpsilonEridani/QFT/Scattering/DIS/SIDIS/Basic.lean:42`: `Factorization.DIS.loChannel C f i x Q2 * D h i zHad Q2` — the fragmentation function is evaluated pointwise. The theorem at Coefficient.lean:499-500 states `doubleConvStructureFunction C f D h x z Q2 = sidisStructureFunction C' f D h x z Q2`, an equality of values, not of one variable's dependence. The module docstring (lines 47-52) explains the obstruction on the parton side only and never says the existing interface has no fragmentation convolution.
findings.fix: Retitle to e.g. "**Compatibility with `sidisStructureFunction` for a coefficient function whose delta sits in the fragmentation variable**", and add the one sentence that makes the result intelligible: `Scattering.DIS.SIDIS.sidisChannel C f D h i x z Q2 = loChannel C f i x Q2 * D h i z Q2` has no convolution in `z`, so `δ(1-w)` matches it exactly while the parton side carries the hard kernel.
findings.issue: "**Compatibility with `sidisStructureFunction` in the fragmentation variable.**" (and the same wording at line 472 for the single channel, and the module-docstring bullet at lines 40-45, "in the fragmentation variable only") suggests the two expressions agree only in their z-dependence. The theorem proves full equality of the two structure functions on (0,1]²; the restriction is on the shape of the coefficient function (`b_i(y) δ(1-w)`), not on the variable.

summary: Documentation is otherwise thorough and accurate (counterexample values, closed forms, and cited declarations all check out), but the three docstrings describing compatibility with `sidisStructureFunction` are headlined "in the fragmentation variable", which reads as a partial equality, and never state the fact that explains the result: `sidisChannel` has no convolution in `z` at all.
